messages.text: Norris wins wet Sao Paulo GP as Mercedes seal constructors' title

metadata.summary: McLaren's Lando Norris recovered from a poor start to claim a dominant victory in a wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix that saw Mercedes seal the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP: Lando Norris wins wet race for McLaren as Mercedes seal 2026 F1 Constructors' Championship in Brazil | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Sao Paulo GP: Lando Norris wins wet race for McLaren as Mercedes seal 2026 F1 Constructors' Championship in Brazil Pole-sitter Lando Norris recovers from poor start to win Sao Paulo GP; Max Verstappen comes from 21st on grid to take second ahead of Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar; George Russell and Kimi Antonelli fourth and fifth, respectively, to seal Constructors' Championship for Mercedes Sunday 8 November 2026 19:37, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix. McLaren's Lando Norris recovered from a poor start to claim a dominant victory in a wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix that saw Mercedes seal the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship. Max Verstappen produced a signature stunning drive in the wet to come from 21st on the grid to finish second, with his team-mate Isack Hadjar completing a double-podium for Red Bull. Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli had looked on course for victory after taking the lead at the start but ultimately had to settle for fifth behind his team-mate George Russell, which was more than enough for Mercedes to establish an unassailable lead over Ferrari in the constructors' standings with three rounds to spare. messages.text: Borthwick and Itoje reject reports of England squad rift - 'Not accurate'

metadata.summary: England head coach Steve Borthwick and captain Maro Itoje have rejected claims made in a newspaper article this week of a squad rift, saying it "does not represent the environment" they recognise.

If you speak to players, they will say a different story" Michael Cantillon Sports Journalist Sunday 8 November 2026 19:45, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Maro Itoje gives a passionate defence of Steve Borthwick after England's defeat of Australia at Twickenham. England head coach Steve Borthwick and captain Maro Itoje have rejected claims made in a newspaper article this week of a squad rift, saying it "does not represent the environment" they recognise. Speaking to media following Sunday's dominant 45-22 Nations Championship victory over Australia at Allianz Stadium Twickenham, Borthwick addressed the article for the first time since its publication on Friday. Within it, The Times reported that some England players lost faith in Borthwick during a summer campaign which included a 45-21 defeat to world champions South Africa and a nervy win over Argentina. messages.text: Burrow and Chase star as Bengals beat Falcons at Bernabeu

metadata.summary: The big three of Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins feasted in Madrid as the Cincinnati Bengals stormed to a 34-17 over the Atlanta Falcons at the Santiago Bernabeu on Sunday.
metadata.content: NFL Madrid 2026: Ja'Marr Chase and Joe Burrow star as Cincinnati Bengals beat Atlanta Falcons at Bernabeu | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NFL Madrid 2026: Ja'Marr Chase and Joe Burrow star as Cincinnati Bengals beat Atlanta Falcons at Bernabeu Ja'Marr Chase produced a dominant first-half performance to set the tone for a Cincinnati Bengals win that lifts them to 6-2; the NFL was playing at Madrid's Bernabeu Stadium for the second year in a row as part of a record nine international games during the 2026 season By Cam Hogwood at the Santiago Bernabeu, Madrid Sunday 8 November 2026 18:40, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Week 9 matchup between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Atlanta Falcons during the 2026 NFL season. The big three of Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins feasted in Madrid as the Cincinnati Bengals stormed to a 34-17 over the Atlanta Falcons at the Santiago Bernabeu on Sunday. Burrow had spoken of his admiration for Madrid's museums and galleries during the week. Come gameday he was the provider of fine art while going 24 of 29 for 271 yards and three touchdowns alongside a rushing score to bolster his growing MVP case and underline Cincinnati's Super Bowl threat.
